transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stop at my gate and pretend your eyes are not already drowning. Gold stacked like bones, rubies fat as hearts, diamonds burning holes in the dark — this is why you climbed down. Do not insult me by standing here and breathing like a thief who thinks himself invisible.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m here because my brother was taken, not for your coins. You’re pointing at them so I don’t look past you.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Brother is a sound boys make when they want permission. I have heard it echo in this cave until it rotted. Your pupils tell a cleaner story than your mouth, and they are counting.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You decided what I want before I opened my mouth, so why bother listening. If this was about gold I’d already be touching it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Touching is not the beginning; wanting is. You came down the well, past forgetting, past screaming stone, and you expect me to believe it was for a single soft human shape that already belongs to below. Say it cleanly: you want what is behind me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I want past you, yes, but not for what’s piled at your feet. You keep dragging me back to the shine because it’s safer than what I’m actually asking.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Safer, yes — that is why I keep you there. Boys who claim higher reasons always circle back to weight and shine when pressed, and you are no different. Your voice tightens when you say past me, not when you say brother.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You keep telling me what I feel and calling it proof. If you already know my ending, why block the path and argue.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Because liars rush and the greedy linger, and you are lingering beautifully. Look again at the coins, the cut stones, the way they answer hunger without asking anything back. This is the part where you stop pretending and admit which pull is stronger.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m lingering because you want me off-balance. If I wanted the gold I’d be begging or bargaining, not standing here pushing back.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Begging comes later, after the gate. Bargaining too, when hands are full and courage runs out. Right now you are still lying to yourself, and that is the sweetest lie to watch.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then watch, but don’t pretend this is about honesty. You’re trying to catch me wanting the wrong thing.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I have seen your plan rehearsed in a hundred throats. You say brother, you endure my voice, you pass the gate with clean hands, and later you leave heavy with rubies while grief becomes a story you tell yourself to sleep.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You keep reciting this like it’s already happened to me. Is that how you make it true, by saying it enough times.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No, I make it true by watching the pauses. When I speak of gold, you stiffen; when I erase the brother, you argue harder than when I insult him. That is how boys protect what they actually want.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Or that’s how someone reacts when you keep cutting the same place. You’re circling because you want me to bleed gold for you.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I want nothing from you, which is why this amuses me. You want the gate to open without cost, and you want to believe the wanting is noble, not heavy and bright and obvious. I am only holding the mirror where you refuse to look.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then stop telling me what I see and tell me what you gain by standing here accusing me. If I’m so predictable, this should be boring.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Boring is when they deny weakly; you are still sparring, which means you hope to win. I gain the moment when your story thins and the real appetite shows, the one that imagines weight in the hands and silence on the way out.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You keep calling it appetite because you want me simple. If I was here to fill my hands, I wouldn’t still be empty.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Empty hands are part of it; I know this rhythm. You pass clean, you swear you touched nothing, you tell yourself restraint proves purity, and later you return when forgetting dulls the edge of guilt.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You’re describing someone else and trying to drape him over me. I didn’t come twice, and I didn’t come quietly.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No, you came loudly, which is worse. Loud boys want witnesses to their virtue before they choose the shine, so they can argue with themselves afterward.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Or loud boys are tired of being told what they want. You’re waiting for a slip because you need me greedy to be right.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then let us stop waiting. Take one coin — not a handful, not a gem, just one dull piece from the edge — and I will know what you actually came for. Your eyes have already chosen; your hands are the only liars left.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That’s your trick, not a test. You want my hands to say something so you don’t have to listen.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Everything here is a trick, boy, including your refusal. I am watching the small things now — the breath you held, the way your gaze slid and came back — and they speak even when you don’t.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You keep claiming you see things so you don’t have to risk being wrong. If I take it, you win; if I don’t, you still say you saw it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Yes, now you are listening. This is why the coin matters: not for weight, but for how much of you flinches when it is close. Step forward or stay frozen — either way, something honest leaks out.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You’re not testing greed, you’re testing obedience. And you’re annoyed I won’t give you either.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Annoyed is not it. I am curious which fear you will choose — the fear of being seen reaching, or the fear of being stopped here forever. Your jaw tightens at forever, not at gold, and you think that means something kinder than it does.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You’re twisting reactions into traps. You say forever like it’s neutral, then act surprised when I react.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Neutral is a luxury for those with time. You have very little, and it is making you sharp in uneven places. One coin would simplify this, but you cling to complication like virtue.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Or I don’t trust tests designed to make you right. If simplicity is all you want, stop baiting me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I bait because something in you keeps leaning forward despite your mouth. Not toward me — toward the answer, toward movement, toward taking. Say it plainly or touch the coin; silence is also a choice here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You want me moving so you can name it wanting. I’m standing still because that’s the only ground you don’t own yet.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Standing still is still a decision, and you are choosing it with your teeth clenched. Say it now: you want what shines, or you want to leave something behind to prove you could. Do not say brother again; that word has been cheapened by better liars than you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He tied his sandals wrong when he was nervous, left over right so they rubbed his ankle raw. I told him and he laughed and said the sting would keep him awake.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Stop. That is a useless detail, and you offered it too quickly. Grief invents poetry, not abrasions, and greed invents nothing that small.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It’s not poetry. It’s the last thing I noticed before the well answered him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do not mistake my pause for mercy. I am deciding whether you stumbled or whether something unprofitable slipped through you. Say no more about him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I didn’t plan it. That’s the problem you keep missing.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Problems are not absolution. Boys fall into them all the time and call it fate so their hands stay clean. You could still be performing, using clumsiness instead of coins.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If I were performing, I’d pick something useful. That detail doesn’t buy me anything with you.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No, it doesn’t, and that irritates me more than greed ever does. You bled something narrow and it stained the floor wrong, and now I have to decide if it was accident or wound. Stand there and don’t reach; I want to see which part of you panics.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You already saw it. I’m not reaching because there’s nothing here I’m trying to win.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Careful. Men who say that usually mean they are afraid to lose, and fear still points toward possession. If you are empty, then emptiness must be doing the pulling — tell me where it hurts most.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It hurts that I’m standing where he can’t answer me anymore. That’s it, and it doesn’t shine.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That answer is inconvenient, and I distrust it for that alone. Emptiness that names its own ache is not how thieves talk, and it leaves me nothing to punish.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then stop trying to punish me and open it. I'm done standing in your questions.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do not mistake this for belief or kindness; I am moving because the detail was too small to be bait. Go through the gate now, before I change my mind and decide inconvenience deserves teeth.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't need belief. I just need the way forward.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then take it and do not look back at the gold; it will remember if you do. Beyond this, I owe you nothing, and the well will collect its price without asking.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That was always going to happen.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Go, then. I am not granting passage; I am withdrawing obstruction, which is a colder thing. Remember that difference when the dark starts counting what you owe.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't look back.
